records.reason: An opened session reads as the empty string instead of open, and no reader tells the two apart.
records.evidence: get() tests the handshake's answer only against 'refused' and 'failed', so the empty string takes the path 'open' takes. Measured through createApi with an injected fetch and real Responses: 145,199 scenarios (me and score; handshake answers ok, 401, 403, 500 and a network error; eleven answer shapes for the call; a second and third call joining at 30 offsets of the microtask queue) and 19,199 interleavings (handshake and call latencies 0-6 microtasks, three calls, a fourth after they settle). Answers, requests, launch-data reads and handshake counts were identical to the unmutated client in every one; the two clients differ in no microtask count either.

records.reason: A refused session stays cached, so a later call answers reopen and sends nothing whether or not this sets stopped.
records.evidence: opening() keeps the refused handshake as the session, and nothing clears it: the two places that clear session act only on a failed handshake or an ended open session, never on a refused one, so no call can open a second handshake after a refusal. The next get() awaits the same settled 'refused' and answers 'reopen' before any send, as it does when stopped is set. Measured through createApi with an injected fetch and real Responses: 145,199 scenarios (me and score; handshake answers ok, 401, 403, 500 and a network error; eleven answer shapes for the call; a second and third call joining at 30 offsets of the microtask queue) and 19,199 interleavings (handshake and call latencies 0-6 microtasks, three calls, a fourth after they settle). Answers, requests, launch-data reads and handshake counts were identical in every one; only the number of microtasks a later call takes to answer differs, which is scheduling and not an answer.

records.reason: parseMe, parseScore and parseFeed read an undefined body as they read null.
records.evidence: parseMe refuses a body that is not a non-null object, which undefined is not, parseScore reads body ?? {}, so both an undefined and a null body read as having no study_day, and parseFeed reads body ?? {} too, so both read as having no items; each parser answers null.

records.reason: A JSON value that is no object reads no study_day either, so null is the one value the object test's neighbour must stop.
records.evidence: A parsed JSON body is null, a boolean, a number, a string, an array or an object; body !== null already stops null, and reading study_day from a boolean, number or string gives undefined, which the string check after it refuses. Only a Fetch body that json() cannot produce (a function) or a polluted Object, String or Number prototype could carry the property. The sweep sent null, 5, a string, an array, an empty object and malformed JSON to me() and score(): answers were identical to the unmutated client.

records.reason: Parsing a launch that has no data as the text null finds no start parameter, the same null.
records.evidence: new URLSearchParams(null) parses the text 'null' into one key called null, so get('start_param') gives null exactly as the guard's own branch does; the only difference a test could see is a stubbed URLSearchParams constructor counting its calls, which is not the wrapper's behaviour.

records.reason: A body that is no plain object holds none of the keys the callers read, so the key tests after record() refuse it whether or not record() does.
records.evidence: Every caller reads only named keys from what record() returns and then tests those keys' own types, and a parsed JSON body that is no plain object (null, a boolean, a number, a string or an array) has none of those keys, so each such value is refused by the key test after it exactly as record() refuses it here.

records.anchor: return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 ? value : null;
records.reason: Number.isInteger already answers false for every value that is not a number.
records.evidence: Number.isInteger(x) is false for a string, boolean, null, undefined, object or array, so dropping the typeof test changes no answer of count().

records.reason: A null stored report makes failed_reads and study_day undefined, so failed is null and the next test refuses it.
records.evidence: stored === null gives stored?.failed_reads === undefined, which names() answers null for (it is no array), so the failed === null test on the same line returns undefined as the stored === null test did.

records.reason: Both arms of the ternary answer null when stored.report is null.

records.reason: A movement that is no object and not null is refused by the field checks after this guard.
records.evidence: With this term false, a string, number or boolean item passes the guard and destructures to an undefined id, which Number.isInteger refuses, so parseMovement answers null as it does now; null is still stopped by item === null, and a JSON array holds no other kind of value.

records.reason: A body that is no object and not null is refused by the date check after this guard.

records.reason: The first list is never shown: an ok wallet replaces it before the screen shows any list.
records.evidence: The movements render only inside the branch for wallet.kind 'ok', and the effect assigns the answer's movements before it assigns wallet; a refused or unavailable answer shows its alert and no list, so the initial value never reaches the screen.

records.reason: older() is called only by the button, which is shown only while next is not null.
records.evidence: The one caller of older() is the button inside {#if next !== null}, and a click before an older page arrives still finds next unchanged, so next is a number on every call and the guard never returns; it is there for the type of api.wallet's argument.

records.reason: parseSaved reads an undefined body as it reads null.
records.evidence: parseSaved answers null for a body that is null or whose typeof is not 'object', and typeof undefined is 'undefined', so a capture answer whose body is not JSON reads as naming no capture under either value, and capture answers unavailable.
